body:
I used to be quiet and shy when I was a child.
My homeroom teacher told me one day that she
was putting on a play for our school festival. ⓐ그
녀는 제가 작은 역할을 하나 맡을 것을 제안하셨고, 연극
에 참여하는 것이 좋은 경험일 거라고 말씀하셨습니다.
So, I decided to do it. I was so (A)[nervous / relaxed]
at the first rehearsal that I could not say my lines
at all. However, as I practiced my lines more, I became
(B)[less and less / more and more] confident. On
the day of the performance, I got anxious and my
mind went blank just before I stepped on the
stage. My classmates tapped me on the shoulder
and (C)[encouraged / discouraged] me. Thanks to
this, I was able to perform my lines perfectly.

(A)
(B)                 (C)
solution: (A) 글쓴이가 자신의 대사를 전혀 말할 수 없었다는 내용이 뒤 에 이어지므로, 이에 대한 원인으로서 글쓴이가 첫 예행연습 때 너무 긴장했다는 흐름이 되는 nervous(긴장한)가 알맞다. (B) 글쓴이가 자신의 대사를 전혀 말할 수 없었다는 내용 다음 에 역접의 접속부사 However(하지만)에 연결된 대조적인 내용 이 이어져야 하므로, 글쓴이가 대사를 더 많이 연습할수록 점 점 더 자신감이 생겼다는 흐름이 되는 more and more(점점 더)가 알맞다. (C) 글쓴이의 반 친구들이 자신의 어깨를 두드리며 격려해 준 덕분에 자신의 대사를 완벽하게 해낼 수 있었다는 흐름이 적 절하므로, encouraged(~을 격려했다)가 알맞다.

M: Hello, Sandra. What brings you here?
G: Hi, Mr. Brown. I got the results from the career
test, but I’m feeling worried because I don’t
know what to do.

career in nursing, but I want to be a teacher. I

volunteer at a local hospital and teach young
children after school.
G: That sounds like a good idea. I’ll give both of
them a try.

through these experiences.

When I was fourteen, I was hospitalized for several
weeks. One day, I saw a piece of paper on the
table. I was (A)[bored / excited], so I picked it up
and began writing things down to pass the time. I
felt a sense of relief when I wrote what I wanted to
do after leaving the hospital. That evening, I asked
my mother to buy me a notebook. As I filled page
after page, I realized that writing was more than
just a way to kill time. As the years passed, my
passion for writing grew (B)[weaker / stronger]. So I
started writing short stories and sharing them with
my friends and family. I felt a sense of (C)[failure /
accomplishment] whenever they told me my stories
were good.
(A)
(B)              (C)
solution: (A) 시간을 때우기 위해 종이 위에 끄적거리기 시작했다는 내 용이 언급되므로, 글쓴이가 병원에 입원해 있으면서 지루했다 는 흐름이 되는 bored(지루한)가 알맞다. (B) 글쓴이가 단편 소설들을 쓰고 그것들을 친구들과 가족들에 게 공유하기 시작했다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 해가 지남에 따라 글쓰기에 대한 글쓴이의 열정이 더 강해졌다는 흐름이 되는 stronger(더 강한)가 알맞다. (C) 글쓴이가 친구들과 가족들에게 자신의 이야기가 훌륭하다 고 들을 때의 반응에 해당하므로, 성취감을 느꼈다는 흐름이 되는 accomplishment(성취)가 알맞다.

body:
Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this (A)expert architect
was once troubled when designing an amusement
park. He finished most of the main structures
except for the pathways between the attractions.
Gropius wanted to find the best design for the
pathways but could not come up with anything that
satisfied him.
One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye
because there was no one selling grapes but only a
box by the side of the road. It turned out that the
elderly couple who owned the vineyard were (B)in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
themselves. Instead, they let people pick as many
grapes as they wanted as long as they put five
francs in the box. The couple not only prevented
their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting
grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable
experience for their customers.
ⓐGropius는 고객들이 자유롭게 포도를 딸 수 있게
허용한 노부부의 아이디어에 깜짝 놀랐기 때문에,
Gropius는 이 발상을 놀이공원 디자인으로 확장하여
방문객들이 그들만의 통행로를 만들도록 허용하는 것
이 좋겠다고 생각했습니다. (C)Upon returning to his
project, he instructed the construction team to plant
grass in areas where he wanted to create the
pathways. When the grass started to grow, he
opened the amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some wide and
some narrow, because they were formed naturally
by visitors. The following year, Gropius used the
grass pathways as an outline on which he built
permanent
pathways,
(D)resulting
in
the
most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
was later chosen as the best road design at the
1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium
in London.
It (E)was contrary to common sense to allow
people to walk on newly sprouted grass because it
could
damage
the
grass.
Moreover,
it
was
unprecedented for an architect to let people do the
designing. Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into
creating ideal pathways by thinking outside the box.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)를 아래와 같이 바꾸어 쓸때 알맞지 않은 것은?
solution: (D) ‘result in ~’은 ‘(결과로) ~을 발생시키다, ~을 초래하다’라는 뜻으로 결과를 나타낼 때 사용하는 표현이며, ‘arise from ~’은 ‘~로부터 발생하다’라는 뜻으로 원인을 나타내는 표현이므로, resulting in을 반대 의미가 되는 arising from으로 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다. 참고로, ‘result in ~’과 유사한 의미의 표현으로 ‘lead to ~(~로 이어지다)’, ‘bring ~ about(~을 가져오다)’, ‘give rise to ~(~을 일으키다, ~을 초래하다)’ 등을 쓸 수 있다.

solution: (A) 앞서 회사가 고지방의 패스트푸드 때문에 건강에 부정적인 영향을 미치는 것에 관한 대중의 비난을 염려했다고 했으며, 뒤에는 고객에게 햄버거와 같은 패스트푸드를 너무 자주 먹지 말라고 말리는 접근법을 대안으로 선택했다는 내용이 이어지 므로, 회사가 대중의 비난을 반박하고 자사의 음식이 건강에 좋다고 주장하는 대신 다른 방식을 시도했다는 흐름으로 nutritious(영양가가 높은)가 알맞다. Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
regarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this expert architect was

Gropius wanted to find the best design for the
pathways but could not come up with anything that
satisfied him.
One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to ⓑwas famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye

box by the side of the road. It turned out that the
elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
themselves. Instead, they let people pick as ⓒmany
grapes as they wanted as long as they put five
francs in the box. The couple not only prevented
their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting
grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable
experience for their customers.

customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it
would be good to extend this idea to the
amusement park design and ⓓallow visitors to
create their own paths. Upon returning to his
project, he instructed the construction team to plant
grass in areas where he wanted to create the
pathways. When the grass started to grow, he
opened the amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some ⓔwidely
and some narrow, because they were formed
naturally by visitors. The following year, Gropius
used the grass pathways as an outline ⓕwhere he
built permanent pathways, resulting in the most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
was later chosen as the best road design at the
1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium
in London.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people

damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented

Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating
ideal pathways by thinking outside the box.

Walter Gropius was a well-known architect, widely
ⓐregarded as one of the pioneers of modernist
architecture. However, even this expert architect was
once troubled when designing an amusement park.
He finished most of the main structures except for
the pathways between the attractions. Gropius wanted
to find the best design for the pathways but could
not come up with anything that satisfied him.
(A) In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The
shapes of the paths were not unified, with
some wide and some narrow, because they
were formed naturally by visitors. The following
year, Gropius used the grass pathways as an
outline ⓑwhich he built permanent pathways,
resulting in the most convenient and efficient
routes. This pathway design was later chosen as
the best road design at the 1971 International
Landscape Architecture Symposium in London.
(B) ⓒAstonished by the elderly couple’s idea of
allowing
customers
to
freely
pick
grapes,
Gropius thought it would be good to extend
this idea to the amusement park design and
allow visitors to create their own paths. Upon
returning to his project, he instructed the
construction team ⓓplant grass in areas where
he wanted to create the pathways. When the
grass
started
to
grow,
he
opened
the
amusement park earlier than planned.
(C) One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to ⓔbeing famous for its vineyards.
Farmers were selling grapes along the road near
each vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his
eye because there was no one selling grapes
but only a box by the side of the road. It
turned out that the elderly couple who owned
the vineyard were in poor health and could not
pick the grapes themselves. Instead, ㉠그들은 사
람들이 그 상자에 5프랑을 넣는 한 그들이 원하는
만큼 많은 포도를 따는 것을 허락했습니다. The
couple not only prevented their grapes from
becoming too ripe by permitting grape picking,
but they also provided an enjoyable experience
for their customers.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people
to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could
damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented
for an architect ⓕto let people do the designing.
Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into creating
ideal pathways by ㉡__________________________________.

위 주어진 글에 이어질 순서로 알맞은 것은?
solution: 숙련된 건축가인 Gropius가 처했던 문제점으로, 놀이기구 사이 의 통행로에 맞는 최적의 디자인을 떠올릴 수 없었다는 주어 진 글 다음에, Gropius가 프랑스 여행 중 건강이 좋지 않아 포 도를 직접 딸 수 없었던 포도원 주인인 노부부가 사람들에게 (길가에 있는) 상자에 5프랑을 넣는 한 원하는 만큼 포도를 마 음껏 따가도록 한 사실을 알게 되었다는 (C), 앞서 언급된 포 도를 직접 따게 하는 일을 the elderly couple’s idea로 가리켜, Gropius가 이 발상을 확장하여 놀이공원의 통행로를 방문객들 이 만들게 하겠다는 생각으로 건축 팀에게 길을 내고자 한 곳 에 잔디를 심도록 지시했고, 잔디가 자라기 시작했을 때 놀이 공원을 개장했다는 (B), 그가 사람들이 반복적으로 걸어 다닌 곳의 잔디 위에 생긴 오솔길을 윤곽선으로 사용하여 영구적인 통행로를 만들었다는 (A)로 이어지는 것이 자연스럽다.

One day, Gropius took a trip to France. The place
he went to was famous for its vineyards. Farmers
were selling grapes along the road near each
vineyard. Then, one far ahead caught his eye
because there was no one selling grapes but only a
box by the side of the road. It turned out that the
elderly couple who owned the vineyard were in
poor health and could not pick the grapes
themselves. Instead, they let people pick as many
grapes as they wanted as long as they put five
francs in the box. The couple not only prevented
their grapes from becoming too ripe by permitting
grape picking, but they also provided an enjoyable
experience for their customers.
Astonished by the elderly couple’s idea of allowing
customers to freely pick grapes, Gropius thought it
would be good to extend this idea to the
amusement park design and allow visitors to create
their own paths. Upon returning to his project, he
instructed the construction team to plant grass in
areas where he wanted to create the pathways.
When the grass started to grow, he opened the
amusement park earlier than planned.
In places where people repeatedly walked, small
footpaths started to form on the grass. The shapes
of the paths were not unified, with some wide and
some narrow, because they were formed naturally
by visitors. The following year, Gropius used the
grass pathways as an outline on which he built
permanent
pathways,
resulting
in
the
most
convenient and efficient routes. This pathway design
was later chosen as the best road design at the
1971 International Landscape Architecture Symposium
in London.
It was contrary to common sense to allow people
to walk on newly sprouted grass because it could
damage the grass. Moreover, it was unprecedented
for an architect to let people do the designing.
Nonetheless, Gropius gained insight into _____________
__________________________ by thinking outside the box.
choices: avoiding public involvement in design decisions
maintaining fixed pathways throughout the park

functions as a “biological supermarket.” Many birds
and mammal species rely on the Everglades for
food, water, and shelter, particularly during the
migration and breeding seasons. For example, the
Florida panther has flourished in the Everglades. It
was nearly extinct in 1995, with only a dozen adults
estimated in the wild. But the whole population in
the Everglades National Park had recovered to
about 230 by 2017.
What is more, the Everglades is the only place
(B)[where / what] American crocodiles and American
alligators coexist. These animals typically inhabit
different ecosystems: crocodiles live in salt water,
whereas alligators live in fresh water. However, they
are found living together where fresh water from
Lake Okeechobee meets the salt water of Florida
Bay. Besides, the Everglades provides drinking water
to people in Florida, with one out of every three
people (C)[rely / relying] on the Everglades for
drinking water. ⓐEverglades가 보존되지 않으면, 수백

In the Sudd, there are many endangered mammal species, including African elephants and antelopes. Additionally, one million people rely on the wetland for a living, primarily through cattle herding. The Camargue is a region in southern France
where the Rhône River meets the Mediterranean
Sea, just a few miles from the city of Arles. It
functions as a natural sponge, absorbing and
gradually releasing surface water such as rain,
groundwater, and floodwater. Its ability to hold
water aids in flood control. The Camargue is also
an excellent place to observe more than 400
species of birds. Due to the fact that wetlands and
lakes cover 35% of the area, the Camargue is an
ideal place for flocks of birds to feed and cool off.
The exotic pink flamingo is one of the most famous
species found there. The area is also known
historically for its white horses. The Camargue
horses are a special breed, said to be one of the
world’s oldest, and they have spent thousands of
years living in the unique environment of the
Camargue and adapted to its salty wetlands. They
have become powerful and strong as a result of
surviving in the Camargue, where only reeds, thick
grasses, and weeds are available. (A)물속을 달리는
말들의 웅장한 모습을 본 적이 있다면, 그들은 이 지
역의 Camargue의 말일 가능성이 매우 높습니다.

All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
ⓐwhat people value.
(A) Cultures with high uncertainty avoidance are
uncomfortable with unexpected or unknown
events. Thus, they tend to have strict standards
and guidelines ⓑto prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures
with low uncertainty avoidance are more open
to the unknown and show more acceptance to
things that are different. This is why these
cultures tend to impose fewer regulations.
(B) Another feature that distinguishes cultures ⓒare
their orientation of temporal horizon, or how they
relate to time. Cultures with short-term orientation
emphasize the present over the future. Since
they are more focused on what is happening now,

features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
what people value. A psychologist named Geert
Hofstede became interested in cataloging these
ⓐinvisible cultural features, and he came up with a
number of categories. According to him, a cultural
difference can be found regarding uncertainty
avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers to how well
people of a certain culture (A)[tolerate / tolerating]
the unexpected. Cultures with high uncertainty
avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or
unknown events. Thus, they tend to have ⓑstrict
standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures with
low uncertainty avoidance (B)[is / are] more open to
the unknown and show more acceptance to things
that are different. This is why these cultures tend to
impose ⓒmore regulations. Another feature (C)[that
/ what] distinguishes cultures is their orientation of
temporal horizon, or how they relate to time.
Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the
present over the future. Since they are more
focused on what is happening now, they place
more stress on having ⓓimmediate outcomes.
However, cultures with long-term orientation value
the future over the present. In these cultures,
people are ⓔlikely to delay short-term results in
favor of long-term ones.

All cultures are different from one another. They
have their unique characteristics. While some of the
features are visible, such as what language people
use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like
what people value. A psychologist who (A)[named /
was named] Geert Hofstede became interested in
cataloging these invisible cultural features, and he
came up with a number of categories. According to
him, a cultural difference can be found regarding
uncertainty avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers
to how well people of a certain culture tolerate the
unexpected.
Cultures
with
high
uncertainty
avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or
unknown events. Thus, they tend to have strict
standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things
from happening. On the other hand, cultures with
low uncertainty avoidance are more open to the
unknown and (B)[show / shows] more acceptance to
things that are different. This is why these cultures
tend to impose fewer regulations. Another feature
that distinguishes cultures is their orientation of
temporal horizon, or how they relate to time.
Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the
present over the future. Since they are more
focused on (C)[that / what] is happening now, they
place more stress on having immediate outcomes.
However, cultures with long-term orientation value
the future over the present. In these cultures,
people are likely to delay short-term results in favor
of long-term ones.

(A)
(B)
(C)
solution: (A) 주격 관계대명사 who가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이므로 선 행사에 수와 태를 일치시켜야 하며, 선행사인 A psychologist 가 Geert Hofstede라고 ‘이름이 붙여진’ 대상이고, 뒤에 ‘name+목적어+목적격보어(명사)(~를 …라고 이름 짓다)’의 목 적어 없이 목적격보어인 Geert Hofstede가 바로 이어지므로, 수동 표현인 ‘~ be named+명사(~가 …라고 이름 지어지다)’의 수동태 was named가 적절하다. (B) 주어부 cultures with low uncertainty avoidance의 핵심인 복수명사 cultures에 수일치한 복수동사 are와 등위 접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 동사 자리이므로, 복수 동사 show가 적절하다. (C) ‘focus on ~(~에 초점을 맞추다)’의 표현을 이루는 전치사 on의 목적어 자리에서 주어가 없는 불완전한 절(is happening now)을 이끌어 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함하여 ‘~한 것’을 뜻하는 관계대명사 what이 적절하다.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?

Switzerland is very concerned about the welfare of not only humans, but also animals. In fact, it is one of the world’s most animal-friendly countries, earning the support of many animal lovers. In 2008, the Swiss government made it a requirement for social animals that typically live in groups, like goldfish, rabbits, or guinea pigs, to be kept in pairs. In other words, it is illegal to own and raise just one goldfish, one rabbit, or one guinea pig. This law recognizes that social animals will experience loneliness if left alone and considers this to be a case of animal abuse. In my case, I raised two guinea pigs when I was young. When one of them died, I had to get another one. Otherwise, I would have been fined. There are additional laws in place to guarantee animals’ quality of life. For example, Switzerland is known to be the only European country requiring all dogs to be microchipped and registered in the country’s database. This is to stop the illegal trade of dogs. As these laws suggest, you can tell how much Switzerland cares about animal welfare.

body:
All cultures are different from one another. They have their unique characteristics. While some of the features are visible, such as what language people use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like what people value. A psychologist who was named Geert Hofstede became interested in cataloging these invisible cultural features, and he came up with a number of categories. According to him, a cultural difference can be found regarding uncertainty avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers to how well people of a certain culture tolerate the unexpected. Cultures with high uncertainty avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or unknown events. Thus, they tend to have strict standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things from happening. On the other hand, cultures with low uncertainty avoidance are more open to the unknown and show more acceptance to things that are different. This is why these cultures tend to impose fewer regulations. Another feature that distinguishes cultures is their orientation of temporal horizon, or how they relate to time. Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the present over the future. Since they are more focused on what is happening now, they place more stress on having immediate outcomes. However, cultures with long-term orientation value the future over the present. In these cultures, people are likely to delay short-term results in favor of long-term ones.

윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how values and norms influence individual behavior across cultures
differences in human behavior shaped by unseen cultural forces
the process by which visible cultural elements shape social identity
criteria and characteristics for understanding cultural differences
how different societies manage uncertainty and plan for the future

MC: Yes, I remember Singapore as a clean and pleasant country to visit. Sophia, can you tell us about an interesting law in Italy?
Sophia: As you know, people from all over the world visit Rome, the capital of Italy. Unfortunately, some tourists’ actions caused severe damage to the city’s historical monuments. So, the city had to establish a number of laws to protect its numerous historical sites. One of them was to forbid adding a lock to any bridge in Rome. You may have heard that to symbolize their love forever, many couples carve their names on locks and attach them to a bridge. However, as the weight of the locks increases the pressure on bridges, they are no longer permitted. Even the existing ones have been removed since 2012. This law was also introduced in Venice so that locks could no longer damage the famous Rialto Bridge. In addition, people are not allowed to go into the city’s iconic Trevi Fountain. Although you may be tempted to dip your toes into the cool fountain water on a hot summer day, it is illegal to do so. Sitting on Rome’s famed Spanish Steps has also been banned since 2019. If you don’t follow this law, you are made to pay a fine ranging from €250 to €450. All of these laws are committed to protecting the city’s historical monuments.

People are prohibited from going into the Trevi Fountain, even on very hot summer days.
From 2019, people have been forbidden from sitting on the Spanish Steps, and violators must pay fines from 250 to 450 euros.

body:
All cultures are different from one another. They have their unique characteristics. While some of the features are visible, such as what language people use or how they dress, others are quite hidden, like what people value. A psychologist named Geert Hofstede became interested in cataloging these invisible cultural features, and he came up with a number of categories. According to him, a cultural difference can be found regarding uncertainty avoidance. Uncertainty avoidance refers to how well people of a certain culture tolerate the unexpected. Cultures with high uncertainty avoidance are uncomfortable with unexpected or unknown events. Thus, they tend to have strict standards and guidelines to prevent uncertain things from happening. (A)________, cultures with low uncertainty avoidance are more open to the unknown and show more acceptance to things that are different. This is why these cultures tend to impose fewer regulations. Another feature that distinguishes cultures is their orientation of temporal horizon, or how they relate to time. Cultures with short-term orientation emphasize the present over the future. Since they are more focused on what is happening now, they place more stress on having immediate outcomes. (B)________, cultures with long-term orientation value the future over the present. In these cultures, people are likely to delay short-term results in favor of long-term ones.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?

2. (B) 앞: 단기 지향 문화는 현재를 중시한다. 뒤: 장기 지향 문화는 미래를 중시한다. → 대조이므로 Conversely / However가 알맞다.
3. 두 빈칸이 모두 대조인 것은 ⑤뿐이다(③의 For instance는 예시).
따라서 답은 ⑤이다.

This work named A Sunday Afternoon on the
Island of La Grande Jatte was created by Georges
Seurat, the pioneer of Pointillism. It portrays people
looking at the river, reading books, or sitting on
the grass. We can see some animals including a
dog and a monkey as well. The grass on which the
shade falls is painted dark. However, other areas
without shadow are painted bright. This (A)[strong
resemblance / sharp contrast] is pretty impressive.
This work is a representative work of Pointillism. It
is mostly painted with dots instead of dashes or
lines. If you look closer, you will notice that ⓐ______
___________________________________. It also has multiple
distinct colors of dots to represent a single color,
which adds (B)[less / more] vibrancy to the painting.
Take a look at a part of the monkey from the
original picture. Its body is made up of a variety of
different colored dots. However, ⓑ멀리서 보여질 때,
다양한 색의 점들이 광학적으로 합쳐져서 갈색을 만들어
낸다. In the process of creating this work, Seurat kept
studying color composition, analyzing it, and revising
this work. It took him two years to produce this huge
piece because he arranged every single dot with
purpose and intention. Since he created art using
color theory, Seurat is known as a(n) (C)[abstract /
scientific] artist. He himself also said, “Some say
they see poetry in my paintings; I see only science.”

(B) Nonetheless, when viewing digital images, we

perceive them as yellow.
(C) Now, zoom in on the edge of the flower. You

with distinct colors and tones. Each tiny square

also
an
accomplished
scientist.

the
Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as
mutually (A)[exclusive / complementary]. Rather, one

was largely through a scientific approach to art that
da Vinci created the outstanding masterpieces for
which he is famous. One example is the Mona Lisa.
This painting utilizes da Vinci’s scientific knowledge
as well as his magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was
(B)[uninterested in / fascinated by] how a smile
begins to form. So, he evaluated every possible
movement of each part of the face to determine
the origin of nerves that control each facial muscle.
This interest in anatomy allowed him to produce
Mona Lisa’s mysterious smile. He also carefully
positioned the torso, head, and eyes so that each
element is slightly turned, while the eyes still face
the viewer. Hence, we have the perception that the
eyes, which are staring straight out, are looking at
us, even when we are not directly in front of the
painting. Additionally, da Vinci created the illusion

This work named A Sunday Afternoon on the
Island of La Grande Jatte ⓐwas created by Georges
Seurat, the pioneer of Pointillism. It portrays people
looking at the river, reading books, or sitting on
the grass. We can see some animals including a
dog and a monkey as well. The grass ⓑwhich the
shade falls is painted dark. However, other areas
without shadow are painted bright. This sharp
(A)contrast is pretty impressive. This work is a
representative work of Pointillism. It is mostly
painted with dots instead of dashes or lines. If you
look closer, you will notice ⓒwhat there are no
object (B)boundary lines. It also has multiple distinct
colors of dots to represent a single color, which
ⓓadds more vibrancy to the painting.
Take a look at a part of the monkey from the
original picture. Its body is made up of a variety of
different colored dots. However, when ⓔviewing
from a distance, the dots of various colors optically
(C)separate to produce brown. In the process of
creating this work, Seurat kept studying color
composition, analyzing it, and revising this work. It
took him two years ⓕto produce this huge piece
because he arranged every single dot with purpose
and (D)intention. Since he created art (E)using color
theory, Seurat is known as a scientific artist. He
ⓖhimself also said, “Some say they see poetry in
my paintings; I see only science.”

다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

Now, let’s look at another Pointillist painting,
Women at the Well, which (A)[painted / was painted]
in 1892 by Paul Signac, a contemporary of Seurat.
In this work, two individuals are drawing water
from a well with a container. Behind the women
are a lighthouse and boats in the ocean. This
artwork portrays a hot sunny day in southern
France through the contrast of yellow sand and
blue ocean. Upon closer inspection, all the objects
in the picture are composed of small dots. It is
worth (B)[noting / to note] that Signac did not
simply paint the grass green by combining yellow
and blue. Rather, he placed separate dots of yellow,
blue, and green next to each other. Viewers then
perceive the combination of these colors as green.
Signac changed the proportions of these colors to
create the various shades of green.
The era of Pointillism came to an end after the first
half of the twentieth century. However, this new and
scientific method of painting had a great influence
on later art groups. Modern artists have adopted
the basic concept of dots and applied (C)[it / them]
to their works in a variety of shapes and forms.
(A)
(B)
(C)

Leonardo da Vinci is known as one of the most
intelligent ⓐpainters in the history of art. Although
he is best known for his artistic masterpieces, he
was also an accomplished scientist. During the
Renaissance, art and science were not perceived as
mutually exclusive. Rather, one ⓑsaw as informing
upon the other. In fact, it was largely through a
scientific approach to art that da Vinci created the
outstanding masterpieces ⓒwhat he is famous for.
One example is the Mona Lisa. This painting utilizes
da Vinci’s scientific knowledge as well as his
magnificent artistic skills. Da Vinci was fascinated by
how a smile begins to form. So, he evaluated every
possible movement of each part of the face to
determine the origin of nerves that control each
facial muscle. This interest in anatomy allowed him
to produce Mona Lisa’s mysterious smile. He also
carefully positioned the torso, head, and eyes so
that each element is slightly turned, while the eyes
still face the viewer. Hence, we have the perception
ⓓwhich the eyes, which are staring straight out, are
looking at us, even when we are not directly in
front of the painting. Additionally, da Vinci created
the illusion of depth in the painting. The farther the
object is, the smaller the scale, the more subtle the
colors, and ⓔthe less detailed the outlines are.

The idea of using dots to produce another color is not new. Long before digital images were invented, French artists Georges Seurat and Paul Signac used a similar technique to paint their artworks in the 1880s. They were influenced by the color theory a French scientist had developed at the time. They did not use traditional brushstrokes to put paint on the canvas. Instead, they used tiny dots of individual colors to create an image. This technique is called Pointillism. The idea behind it is that when numerous dots of separate colors are placed next to each other, and then viewed from a distance, they blend in the viewer’s eyes. Let’s look at two examples of Pointillist style paintings. In the 1880s, French artists Georges Seurat and Paul Signac utilized ______________ under the influence of ______________ ______________, creating images with many small ______________ of separate ______________ that visually combine in the viewer’s eye when seen from a distance. 천재(조수경) 6과

This work named A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte was created by Georges Seurat, the pioneer of Pointillism. It portrays people looking at the river, reading books, or sitting on the grass. We can see some animals including a dog and a monkey as well. The grass on which the shade falls is painted dark. However, other areas without shadow are painted bright. This sharp contrast is pretty impressive. This work is a representative work of Pointillism. It is mostly painted with dots instead of dashes or lines. If you look closer, you will notice that there are no object boundary lines. It also has multiple distinct colors of dots to represent a single color, which adds more vibrancy to the painting. Take a look at a part of the monkey from the original picture. Its body is made up of a variety of different colored dots. However, when viewed from a distance, the dots of various colors optically merge to produce brown. In the process of creating this work, Seurat kept studying color composition, analyzing it, and revising this work. It took him two years to produce this huge piece because he arranged every single dot with purpose and intention. Since he created art using color theory, Seurat is known as a scientific artist. He himself also said, “Some say they see poetry in my paintings; I see only science.” Georges Seurat’s A Sunday Afternoon on the Island of La Grande Jatte is a masterpiece of _____________, in which carefully arranged dots of various colors visually _____________ to produce a single new color, showing his _____________ use of color theory. 천재(조수경) 6과

painting utilizes da Vinci’s scientific knowledge as

fascinated by how a smile begins to form. So, he
evaluated every possible movement of each part of
the face to determine the origin of nerves that
control each facial muscle. This interest in anatomy

in the painting. The farther the object is, the
smaller the scale, the more subtle the colors, and
